items.title: SCHD’s 0.06% Fee Hides the Real Cost: March’s 31% Reshuffle Sold Two Top-10 Holdings Out From Under Holders
items.summary: SCHD's 0.06% expense ratio gets all the attention, but something that happened quietly in March may have cost dividend investors far more than a decade of fees combined.

items.title: Is HPE Stock Now A Bet On Memory Prices?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) trades near $62, at the top of its 52-week range and up about 160% over the past year. The company just reported record revenue of $12.2 billion for fiscal Q3 2026 and a raised outlook for fiscal 2027. The easy read is that you are early in an AI cycle. The harder question is what paid for it.

items.title: Cisco's New Splunk AI Package Targets Computing Inside the Customer's Walls
items.summary: The release combines infrastructure and software while leaving customers responsible for operating their own deployment.

items.title: Was The HPE Stock Surge Visible In Its Orders?
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) stock has run from about $24 to roughly $62 over the past year, a gain of about 159% against close to 19% for the S&P 500. That move was legible in advance, but only one place told you which way. The order book moved long before the profit line did.

items.title: Should You Buy Dell Technologies Stock For All That AI Revenue?
items.summary: Dell Technologies (DELL) has returned more than 360% over the past year and now sits right at the top of its 52-week range. Measured against sales it is still cheaper than the S&P 500. Measured against the cash it produces, it costs about twice the index. Both readings describe the same company, and the gap is the decision.

items.title: Advanced Micro Devices vs. ASML: Which Tech Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
items.summary: AMD's 34% revenue surge and 12.5% net margin contrast sharply with ASML's 29.4% profitability and $12.3 billion in free cash flow.
